={{ JSON.stringify((() => { const c = $('FlattenClient').first().json; const existing = Array.isArray($json.body) && $json.body.length > 0; const row = { client_id: c.clientId, phone: c.from, source: 'whatsapp', last_contact_at: new Date().toISOString(), updated_at: new Date().toISOString() }; if (!existing) { row.stage = 'new'; row.consent_status = 'unknown'; if (c.profileName) row.full_name = c.profileName; } return row; })()) }}

' (' + a.profileName + ')' : ''), data: { lead_id: a.leadId, source: 'whatsapp', channel: 'twilio_sandbox' } }; })()) }}

nodes.name: IsClaudeRetryable
nodes.notes: Retry once on timeout/5xx only. A 4xx is a config fault - retrying wastes money and time (spec 4.2).

nodes.name: ParseClaude
nodes.notes: Backstop only - the API already enforces the schema. Still required for refusal / max_tokens.

nodes.name: IsReplyUsable
nodes.notes: A malformed or refused response must never reach the lead. Silence plus a logged error is recoverable; a broken reply is not.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ client_id: $json.clientId, lead_id: $json.leadId, channel: 'whatsapp', direction: 'outbound', body: $json.replyText, status: $json.sendOk ? 'sent' : 'failed', ai_generated: true, approved_by_human: null, external_id: $json.twilioSid }) }}

nodes.name: PrepRunAI
nodes.notes: No message bodies or PII in payload (spec 4.2).

nodes.name: PrepRunDuplicate
nodes.notes: Twilio retry - already answered. Must not reply twice.

nodes.name: MergeLeadFields
nodes.notes: The no-backwards rule. A populated field never returns to null. Merges, never assigns.

nodes.name: AfterLeadUpdate
nodes.notes: Reads $('MergeLeadFields') explicitly - $input after an HTTP node is an envelope (lesson 9).

nodes.name: IsNewlyQualified
nodes.notes: Fires on the TRANSITION only. Gated on stageBefore != qualified, so later messages do not re-emit.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify((() => { const j = $json; const l = j.leadAfter || {}; return { client_id: j.clientId, type: 'lead.qualified', severity: 'info', summary: 'Lead qualified: ' + j.from + (l.area ? ' | ' + l.area : '') + (l.budget_max ? ' | up to ' + l.budget_max : ''), data: { lead_id: j.leadId, stage_before: j.stageBefore, stage_after: j.stageAfter, lead_type: l.lead_type, timeline: l.timeline, area: l.area, budget_min: l.budget_min, budget_max: l.budget_max } }; })()) }}

nodes.name: IsLeadEscalated
nodes.notes: Step 1 of §8 enforced on EVERY later message: an escalated lead is stored but never answered.

nodes.name: PrepRunSilenced
nodes.notes: Stored but not answered. No Claude call is made at all - escalation stops spend, not just replies.

nodes.name: IsRetryableReply
nodes.notes: The one malformed reply seen was not reproducible in 8 runs, so a single retry very likely recovers it.

nodes.name: ParseGuardRetry
nodes.notes: Same source as ParseClaude, flagged wasGuardRetry so a second rejection cannot loop.

nodes.name: DecideEscalation
nodes.notes: Triggers: needs_human, budget >= high_value_threshold_eur, or any Claude/parse/guard failure.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify((() => { const d = $('DecideEscalation').first().json; const lu = $('AfterLeadUpdate').first().json; const base = (lu.leadAfter && lu.leadAfter.qualification) || {}; const q = Object.assign({}, base); q.escalated = { at: new Date().toISOString(), reason: d.escalationReason, reasons: d.escalationReasons }; return { qualification: q, updated_at: new Date().toISOString() }; })()) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ client_id: $json.clientId, lead_id: $json.leadId, channel: 'whatsapp', direction: 'outbound', body: ($json.handoffBody || $json.handoffNote), status: $json.handoffOk ? 'sent' : 'failed', ai_generated: false, approved_by_human: null, external_id: $json.handoffSid }) }}

nodes.name: StoreHandoffMessage
nodes.notes: Stores what was actually SENT, not the config template. These diverged the moment the no-availability path started prepending the reply -- and the messages table is what LoadHistory feeds back to Claude, so a divergence gives the model a false memory of its own last message.

nodes.name: AfterNotify
nodes.notes: escalation_notify_failed at critical severity - the alert must not die silently with the channel.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify((() => { const j = $json; const evs = [{ client_id: j.clientId, type: 'lead.escalated', severity: 'warning', summary: 'Escalated ' + j.from + ' - ' + j.escalationReason, data: { lead_id: j.leadId, reasons: j.escalationReasons, handoff_sent: j.handoffOk, operator_notified: j.notifyOk } }]; if (!j.notifyOk) { evs.push({ client_id: j.clientId, type: 'run.failed', severity: 'critical', summary: 'escalation_notify_failed: operator NOT reached for ' + j.from, data: { lead_id: j.leadId, error_type: 'escalation_notify_failed', twilio_error: j.notifyErrorCode, detail: j.notifyErrorMessage, escalation_reason: j.escalationReason } }); } return evs; })()) }}

={{ JSON.stringify((() => { const c = $('AfterLead').first().json.config || {}; const now = new Date(); const end = new Date(now.getTime() + ((c.booking_window_days || 14) * 86400000)); return { timeMin: now.toISOString(), timeMax: end.toISOString(), timeZone: c.timezone || 'Europe/Lisbon', items: [{ id: c.calendar_id || 'MISSING' }] }; })()) }}

nodes.name: QueryFreeBusy
nodes.notes: Runs on every inbound message. It is cheap, and it means the model always has real times to hand if the conversation turns to booking - without a second Claude call.

nodes.name: ProposeSlots
nodes.notes: The workflow chooses the slots, not the model - C2 must be able to match a confirmation against exactly what was offered.
